test_title: PYST 60: SSC MTS 2024 - Numerical and Mathematical Ability (Held On: 13 Nov, 2024 - Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: A retailer announces a discount of 25% for selling a mobile phone marked at ₹48,000. The cost price of the mobile phone is 45% below the marked price. He offers a further discount of 7.5% if the buyer returns his old mobile phone. What is the ratio of the profit percentages of the retailer with the return of the old mobile phone scheme to that of without the return of the old mobile phone, respectively?
solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹48,000

Discount = 25%

Cost Price (CP) = 45% below the Marked Price

Further Discount = 7.5% if the old mobile phone is returned

**Calculation:**

Cost Price: CP = MP × (1 - 45/100)

⇒ CP = ₹48,000 × (1 - 0.45)

⇒ CP = ₹48,000 × 0.55

⇒ CP = ₹26,400

Selling Price without old mobile return: SP (without old mobile return) = MP × (1 - 25/100)

⇒ SP (without old mobile return) = ₹48,000 × (1 - 0.25)

⇒ SP (without old mobile return) = ₹48,000 × 0.75

⇒ SP (without old mobile return) = ₹36,000

Selling Price with old mobile return: SP (with old mobile return) = SP (without old mobile return) × (1 - 7.5/100)

⇒ SP (with old mobile return) = ₹36,000 × (1 - 0.075)

⇒ SP (with old mobile return) = ₹36,000 × 0.925

⇒ SP (with old mobile return) = ₹33,300

Profit without old mobile return: Profit (without old mobile return) = SP (without old mobile return) - CP

⇒ Profit (without old mobile return) = ₹36,000 - ₹26,400

⇒ Profit (without old mobile return) = ₹9,600

Profit Percentage without old mobile return: Profit Percentage (without old mobile return) = (Profit/CP) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage (without old mobile return) = (₹9,600/₹26,400) × 100

Profit with old mobile return: Profit (with old mobile return) = SP (with old mobile return) - CP

⇒ Profit (with old mobile return) = ₹33,300 - ₹26,400

⇒ Profit (with old mobile return) = ₹6,900

Profit Percentage with old mobile return: Profit Percentage (with old mobile return) = (Profit/CP) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage (with old mobile return) = (₹6,900/₹26,400) × 100

Ratio of Profit Percentages = Profit Percentage (with old mobile return) : Profit Percentage (without old mobile return)

⇒ Ratio = [(₹9,600/₹26,400) × 100] / [(₹6,900/₹26,400) × 100]

⇒ Simplified Ratio = 23 : 32

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**
